title: A layer its container cut off can be brought back in one step
goal: A layer that its container has clipped away now wears a mark in the Layers list saying it is out of view, and the tip tells you to move it or to turn Clip contents off. Both of those are several steps away, and the fastest way back today is typing a new Y into the panel. The mark should offer the way back where it already tells you about the problem.
notes: Design review 2026-09-06. Evidence: queue/audits/2026-09-06-out-of-view.json rough 3, There is no one-click way back, and rough 4, the mark lives in the Layers list only. Small follow-up to the marking work that landed the same day; the mark and its tip are RowOutOfView.swift plus OutOfView in the app layer.
acceptance: The row of a layer that is out of view offers a way to bring it back into its container
Taking it puts the layer somewhere visible inside the container, and one undo puts it back where it was
It is offered on a layer inside a screen too, not only inside a group with Clip contents on
A layer that is only half out of view is unchanged, since it is not marked in the first place

log.note: Adversarial review before building. The mark is a status glyph today, and the audit's own evaluate line asks whether it reads as a button; making it pressable risks it reading as a Clip contents toggle. Kept it a bare glyph at rest and gave it a capsule on hover, which is the only moment somebody needs telling. A shut group's mark reports layers it is HIDING, not itself: pressing it does what its tip already advises and opens the group, rather than bulk-moving layers nobody can see. Landing: shortest distance, over the edge it left by, so the axis that was fine keeps the number somebody put there. Centring would throw that away. Cut: no flash, no toast.

Adversarial review on the real app found the mock's assumption is wrong for arranging containers. First build moved the layer with moveLayer(toParentOrigin:), driven through the probe on the starter Card (a column stack held to 120): Body came back in AND the stack reflowed, pushing Title out of view instead. Net zero, plus a silent reorder. So canBringLayerIntoView now defers to LayerGeometryEditing.canMove, the same question the inspector's X and Y ask, which also rules out locked layers. Inside a stack or grid the mark stays a plain glyph and the tip says the container is not big enough. Follow-up filed: a-container-too-small-for-what-is-inside-it-says.

Shipped. PhotonzCore/BringIntoView.swift: OutOfView.landingBox/landing (overlap every clip in force, clamp shortest distance, oversize lands on the corner), PhotonzDocument.clipScopes(around:)/canPlace/bringIntoViewOrigin/canBringLayerIntoView/bringLayerIntoView. RowOutOfView gains canReturn, set by layerRows, so the panel never has to ask the document at body time. App: OutOfViewMark is a Button when there is something to press and a plain glyph otherwise; LayersRow.pressOutOfViewMark; row menu item Bring into View; Layer menu Bring into View on the selection (EditorState.canBringSelectionIntoView/bringSelectionIntoView, one undo step for a mixed selection). 21 new core tests, Scripts/test.sh green at 4348.

Verified live on the probe (Screen Recording granted). Scripts/playtest/bring-into-view-walk.json: screen shrunk past a rectangle -> row marked 'cut off by Frame' -> one press lands it at y 230 flush inside -> every mark gone, layer selected -> one undo puts it back at y 320 with the mark. out-of-view-mark-walk.json re-run confirms the shut Card mark is still a pressable control and the stacked Body mark is now a non-pressable row target. That walk also had a latent failure (it assumed a panel scroll position the probe remembers between runs); added explicit scrollPanel steps.
Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-07-bring-into-view.json with two real window captures.

The orange scissors on an out-of-view row is now the way back: one press slides the layer inside its container (shortest distance, one undo step), and on a shut group the same press opens it. Also on the row's menu and the Layer menu as Bring into View. Not offered inside a stack or grid, where moving one layer only pushes another out; the mark explains the container is too small instead, and a follow-up task is filed. Core in Sources/PhotonzCore/BringIntoView.swift with 21 tests, Scripts/test.sh green at 4348, verified live on the probe with real captures in queue/audits/2026-09-07-bring-into-view.json.
